title: Lead-lag: does US diesel lead European gasoil?

explain.prompt: In 4–6 sentences: what does the table say about ULSD and gasoil (and Brent and gasoil) at lag 1? Give the mechanical explanation, and say whether a trader could exploit it. Why is the same table computed on price levels useless?
rubric: Lag 1 ≈ 0.36 (ULSD → gasoil) and ≈ 0.28 (Brent → gasoil), negative lags ≈ 0: yesterday's NYMEX/Brent move 'predicts' today's gasoil move.

Mechanism: ICE Gasoil settles at 17:30 London, about two hours before Brent (19:30) and NYMEX (14:30 New York); news arriving in between is in today's ULSD and Brent settlements but only in tomorrow's gasoil settlement.

It is a timing artefact of settlement prices, not a causal lead: by the time ULSD settles, gasoil is already trading on the same news; the 'signal' cannot be traded at the settlement prices used to measure it.
Before claiming a lead-lag, check closing times, publication delays and time zones; compare prices taken at the same instant if possible.
On price levels every lag correlates at ≈ 0.95–0.98 because both series trend: the table says nothing about who moves first. Lead-lag is measured on changes.
Choosing the best lag on the whole sample and then 'testing' it on the same data is selection bias.
